subject: physics
title: Key ideas
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Key ideas — AQA GCSE Physics (8463) specification, section 4.9.
meta_desc: GCSE Physics (AQA) practice covering Key ideas, specification section 4.9.
final_note: You worked through Key ideas — 9 specification statements.

concepts.def: One of a small number of ideas used to describe the complex and diverse phenomena of the natural and man-made world. A key idea is a way of thinking that recurs across the whole subject rather than a detail belonging to one topic.

The property of the key ideas that they apply everywhere in the subject content rather than in one topic. Because they are embedded throughout the content, they underpin the assessment and are assessed across all papers.

A simplified representation of a system or process, used to describe, explain and predict behaviour. A model is judged by how well it explains and predicts, not by whether it contains every detail of the real thing.
A model in which matter is treated as a large number of small particles, with the arrangement and motion of those particles used to explain the properties of solids, liquids and gases.

A model in which a phenomenon is treated as a wave, so that quantities such as wavelength, frequency and amplitude can be used. Light is modelled as a transverse wave and sound as a longitudinal wave.
The idea that a change in one quantity produces a particular change in another: a resultant force causes acceleration, and a change inside an atomic nucleus causes a radioactive emission.
A phenomenon in which one object affects another without touching it, such as two magnets repelling, a charged rod attracting paper, or the Earth pulling on the Moon.

A region in which an object experiences a force because of a property it has, such as charge, magnetism or mass. The field concept is the key to analysing electrical, magnetic and gravitational effects.

A difference in a quantity between two places that causes something to change or to flow. A pressure difference drives gas flow, a temperature difference drives energy transfer by heating, and a potential difference drives charge flow.
A relationship in which one quantity changes by the same factor as another, so that the ratio of the two stays constant. Proportionality is an important aspect of many models in science.

The relationship shown by a graph that is a straight line through the origin. Weight is directly proportional to mass, and the extension of a spring is directly proportional to the force applied, up to the limit of proportionality.

The expression of a physical law or model as an equation relating quantities, for example weight = mass × gravitational field strength. The equation states the relationship itself, not merely a recipe for a calculation.

mcqs.q: The specification says that diverse phenomena can be described in terms of a small number of key ideas. Which statement best describes a key idea in physics?
options: A way of thinking that recurs in many topics and describes a wide range of phenomena
An especially large and detailed topic that has to be revised in far more depth
A rule that applies only inside the topic in which it was first taught
A page of background reading that is never used in any examination paper
mcqs.explain: A key idea is valuable because it applies across the whole subject, not because it is detailed.

mcqs.q: The key ideas are of universal application and are embedded throughout the subject content. What does this mean for the examinations?
options: They are examined only in the last question of the final paper
They can be assessed in questions on any topic, on all papers
They are examined only in questions set for the higher tier
They are not examined, as they are not a taught topic
mcqs.explain: The specification states that the key ideas underpin the assessment and are assessed across all papers.

mcqs.q: Which of the following does the specification list as a key idea in physics?
options: Learning the names of all the required practical activities
Quoting every calculated answer to three significant figures
The use of models, such as the particle model of matter
Recalling the names of the SI base units in physics
mcqs.explain: The specification lists the use of models, as in the particle model of matter or the wave models of light and of sound.

mcqs.q: Why is the particle model of matter called a model?
options: Because it is a physical copy of matter built for classroom use
Because it is an idea that no evidence has yet been found for
Because it applies to solids but not to liquids or gases
Because it is a simplified way to explain and predict
mcqs.explain: A model is a simplified representation judged by how well it explains and predicts.

mcqs.q: Light and sound are both described using a wave model. Which statement about these two models is correct?
options: Sound and light are both modelled as longitudinal waves in a medium
Sound is modelled as a longitudinal wave and light as a transverse wave
Sound and light are both modelled as transverse waves on a screen
The wave model is used for light only, as sound is a flow of particles
mcqs.explain: The two wave models differ: sound oscillates along the direction of travel, light across it.

mcqs.q: A car on a straight road has a constant resultant force acting forwards. Using the idea of cause and effect, what is the effect of that force?
options: The car keeps moving at a steady speed while the force acts
The car gains mass steadily while the force is applied
The car accelerates for as long as the force acts on it
The car halts the instant the force is removed
mcqs.explain: A resultant force is the cause and acceleration is the effect.

mcqs.q: A sample of an unstable isotope emits alpha particles. Applying the idea of cause and effect, what is the cause of this emission?
options: A chemical reaction between the outer electrons
The high temperature of the material around it
A collision with a nearby moving atom
A change inside the nucleus of the atom
mcqs.explain: The specification links changes in atomic nuclei to radioactive emissions.

mcqs.q: Two magnets repel each other without touching. Which group of effects does physics analyse using the idea of a field?
options: Electrical, magnetic and gravitational effects
Gravitational, frictional and elastic contact effects
Electrical, magnetic and thermal conduction effects
Magnetic, sound transmission and nuclear effects
mcqs.explain: The specification names these three as the effects analysed using the field concept.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly applies the key idea that differences are the drivers of change?
options: Gas flows out of a cylinder when the gas inside has a large volume
Energy is transferred by heating when an object is at a high temperature
Charge flows through a resistor when there is a potential difference across it
Charge flows through a resistor when a large charge is stored in the cell
mcqs.explain: Potential difference is the electrical case of a difference driving a change.

mcqs.q: The weight of an object is directly proportional to its mass. What does this tell you?
options: A graph of weight against mass is a straight line with a positive intercept
Weight and mass are the same quantity written in different units
Weight rises as mass rises, but not by a fixed multiplying factor
Doubling the mass doubles the weight in the same gravitational field
mcqs.explain: Proportionality means the two quantities change by the same factor, with g as the constant.

mcqs.q: A student loads a spring with increasing weights and finds that extension is directly proportional to force. Which statement about this model is correct?
options: Doubling the force doubles the extension up to the limit of proportionality
Doubling the force doubles the extension for every force applied to the spring
Doubling the force doubles the extension only when the spring is unstretched
Doubling the force halves the extension as the spring becomes stiffer
mcqs.explain: The proportional model holds only within a stated range of validity.

mcqs.q: The specification says that physical laws and models are expressed in mathematical form. Which statement shows this key idea?
options: Rearranging an equation changes the physical law that it describes
weight = mass × gravitational field strength is a relationship
An equation is only a shortcut for doing the arithmetic quickly
A description of a law in words is more precise than an equation
mcqs.explain: The equation expresses the law that weight is proportional to mass, in the form the specification uses.
